# Code review: WA-2952, drop CSP-blocked `EvalError`s from RUM

**How I ran it:** full review of the committed range `c47ad80…HEAD` (`89979c0`) only. Nothing was modified, installed, tested or posted.

**Scope:** 2 files, +110 −0. `apps/web/src/services/observability/providers/datadog.ts` gets +48 and its test file gets +62.

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Fine to open once #1 is fixed or consciously accepted. Nothing blocks. |
| **Score** | 88 / 100 (2 of 5 findings checked by agents) |
| **What held it down** | The "is this our code?" check looks at the whole stack, so it misses noise from vendors that our own code calls into |
| **Fix first** | #1 |

## Scores by area (worst first)

| Area | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Bugs | 80 | #1 |
| Testing | 88 | #2 |
| Conventions | 94 | #3 |
| Simplicity | 95 | #4 |
| Security | 96 | #5 |
| Regression, architecture, performance, duplication | 100 | Nothing found. Only `filterRumEvent` changed and its signature is the same. |

## What this review did not cover

- I did the category passes myself instead of running nine separate agents, because the diff is small. Only #1 and one other candidate went through the paired validate-and-refute check.
- `node_modules` isn't installed here. The finding #1 validator read `@datadog/browser-core` v7.9.0 from another checkout, but this repo pins `^6.24.1`.
- The vendor scripts themselves (HubSpot, Calendly, Beamer, Turnstile) are hosted outside the repo. So I couldn't confirm when their `eval()` calls actually run.

## Fix before opening

### #1: The first-party check matches our bundle anywhere in the stack, so the named vendors' errors aren't dropped
**Bugs · P2 · confirmed (validator 80, refuter couldn't beat it)** · `apps/web/src/services/observability/providers/datadog.ts:90-92`

- **What:** `isNotFirstPartyStack` runs `!stack.includes('_next/static/')` on the whole stack. Datadog's `toStackTraceString` includes every frame, not just the top one.
- **Failure case:** our code sometimes calls straight into a vendor, so our frame ends up under the vendor's frames:
  - `HubSpotForm.tsx:30-32`: `script.onload` calls `window.hbspt.forms.create(...)`, with no try/catch around it.
  - `useCalendly.ts:212` and `services/beamer/index.ts:53` follow the same pattern.
  - In each case the blocked `EvalError` has a `_next/static/chunks/…` frame lower in the stack, so it is **kept**. That is the noise WA-2952 is meant to remove, from vendors the docstring names.
  - `useCaptchaToken.ts:73` (Turnstile) is partly protected by a local try/catch.
- **Consequence:** none for users. The Error-Free Views SLO just keeps some of the noise. The 72 events a month won't fully go away, and it may look like the fix didn't work.
- **Fix:** look only at the frame that threw. That's the first `at …` line that isn't `eval`/`<anonymous>`. Add a test with a vendor top frame and a `_next/static/` caller frame below it.

## Worth a ticket / your call

| # | Area · Priority | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Testing · P3 | `datadog.test.ts:389` | In "drops an EvalError regardless of source", the `'console'` case proves nothing, because `NON_USER_IMPACTING_SOURCES` already drops it. The test doesn't cover a mixed vendor-plus-our-code stack (#1) or a `custom` source. |
| 3 | Conventions · P3 | `datadog.ts:72-111, 157-161` | About 40 comment lines for 3 lines of logic. AGENTS.md says to treat comments as tech debt. Some claims will go stale: "grepped `apps/web/src` and `packages/`" and the vendor list. The trade-off paragraph repeats the commit message. |
| 4 | Simplicity · P3 | `datadog.ts:76-93` | The comment on `isNotFirstPartyStack` is about `error.type`, which is a different concern. The name is also a negation. `isFirstPartyStack` plus `!` at the call site would read more clearly. |
| 5 | Security · P3 | `datadog.ts:174` | The CSP-eval block was the only in-app signal left. `report` events are already dropped, and the CSP has no `report-uri`/`report-to` (`securityHeaders.ts:16-29`). If a vendor script were compromised and tried `eval`, nobody would see it. Consider a `report-to` endpoint or a sampled `addAction` instead of dropping these completely. |

## Worth tidying (no score impact)

1. **Share the stack helper.** `isNotFirstPartyStack` has the same shape as `originatesFromExtension` (`datadog.ts:62-65`). One `stackIncludesAny(stack, patterns)` could serve both. About 6 lines.
2. **Remove `any` from the new tests.** They add 5 more `{} as any` casts (`datadog.test.ts:397, 409, 421, 433, 444`). The file already does this, but AGENTS.md says to never use `any`. A typed `buildErrorEvent` and `emptyContext` helper would remove all of them. About 10 lines.

Fix now, ticket, or skip? Your call. If I don't hear back, I'll skip them.

## Ruled out

- **An `EvalError` we report ourselves (source `custom`) gets dropped silently and makes the docstring wrong** (`datadog.ts:174`). Refuted, and the validator gave only a partial confirmation at confidence 30.
  - The docstring states the "regardless of source" drop right there at `datadog.ts:157-161`.
  - `trackError` always wraps errors in `CodedException`, which reports type `Error`.
  - `captureException` isn't a real function; only two comments mention it.
  - The only raw-error path left is the ErrorBoundary at `_app.tsx:153`. It needs a real first-party `EvalError`, and none exists today.

## Also checked, nothing found

- Production `script-src` really does use `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` only (`securityHeaders.ts:19-22`).
- There are no `eval(` or `new Function(` calls in `apps/web/src` or `packages/`.
- There's no `assetPrefix` or `basePath` that would change the `_next/static/` path.

## Findings list

1. `apps/web/src/services/observability/providers/datadog.ts:90`: P2 bugs, whole-stack first-party check
2. `apps/web/src/services/observability/providers/__tests__/datadog.test.ts:389`: P3 testing, vacuous case and missing mixed-stack test
3. `apps/web/src/services/observability/providers/datadog.ts:72`: P3 conventions, too many comments that will go stale
4. `apps/web/src/services/observability/providers/datadog.ts:76`: P3 simplicity, misplaced docstring and negated name
5. `apps/web/src/services/observability/providers/datadog.ts:174`: P3 security, no CSP signal left
